title: Everything we know about the Louvre jewellery heist
facts: Thieves wielding power tools broke into the Louvre Museum in Paris during broad daylight and stole eight items of jewellery.
Four suspects utilized a vehicle-mounted mechanical lift to access the Louvre's Galerie d'Apollon via a balcony.
Two of the thieves entered the Louvre Museum by cutting through a first-floor window using power tools.
The thieves cut through the glass of two display cases inside the Louvre Museum to steal the jewels.
French police reported the thieves remained inside the Louvre Museum for four minutes before escaping on two waiting scooters at 09:38 local time.
A preliminary report indicated that one in three rooms in the raided area of the Louvre Museum lacked CCTV cameras.
The French culture ministry stated that the Louvre museum's wider alarms activated during the burglary.
A museum staff member intervened to prevent the thieves from setting fire to their vehicle outside the Louvre.
Approximately 60 investigators were assigned to work on the Louvre Museum theft case.
The eight stolen items from the Louvre Museum include 19th-century diadems, necklaces, ear-rings, and brooches.
Empress Eugénie's crown was discovered damaged on the thieves' escape route after apparently being dropped.
Louvre officials requested government assistance earlier in the year to restore aging exhibition halls and enhance artwork protection.
French President Emmanuel Macron pledged to redesign the Louvre Museum as part of the New Renaissance project costing between 700 million and 800 million euros.
Thieves broke into the Adrien Dubouche Museum in Limoges in September 2025 and stole porcelain works valued at 9.5 million euros.
Armed robbers raided the Hieron Museum in Burgundy in November 2024 and stole 20th-century artworks.
